0.long_answer: Papillorenal syndrome is caused by mutations in the PAX2 gene, which plays a critical role in the development of the eye and kidney. The PAX2 gene belongs to the paired box (PAX) gene family. Members of this family are transcription factors that contain a conserved paired domain, making them essential for orchestrating the development of various tissues and organs during embryogenesis. Disruption in the PAX2 gene due to mutations can lead to the clinical features observed in Papillorenal syndrome, including ocular anomalies and renal malformations.
